hero.title: Morning News & Global Update — Thursday, 5 November 2026
hero.description: Nigeria's political landscape moves into a new phase following Atiku Abubakar's ADC campaign launch in Sokoto, a police investigation into the attack on Peter Obi's convoy in Calabar, major government borrowing proposals and progress towards state policing. Around the world, the US midterm results reshape Washington, maritime incidents raise fresh concerns around the Strait of Hormuz, Ukraine reports a mounting civilian death toll, and political and security developments unfold across Europe, Africa and Asia.

morningSummary: Thursday's leading stories include the formal launch of Atiku Abubakar's ADC presidential campaign in Sokoto, the arrest of a suspect following an attack on Peter Obi's convoy in Calabar, Senate scrutiny of President Tinubu's proposed $7.7 billion external borrowing plan, and the transmission of the proposed state police constitutional amendment to the Presidency. In the United States, Democrats have secured control of both chambers of Congress in the 3 November midterm elections. Iran's Revolutionary Guard has reported fires involving two oil tankers and a tugboat in the Strait of Hormuz, although the circumstances remain based on the Iranian military's account. Ukraine says the death toll following a strike on an aid distribution centre in Zaporizhzhia has reached 40. France is preparing for nationwide demonstrations, while a cyberattack affecting refrigeration controls at three French blood-storage facilities was detected before any blood products were compromised. In Africa, Ethiopia has ordered six Sudanese diplomatic staff to leave, and South Africa is counting votes following its municipal elections.
editorialNote: RadiantWaves Media reports independently and distinguishes verified developments from campaign statements, official claims, allegations and opinion. Political promises are not presented as achieved results. Reports concerning attacks, conflict incidents and security allegations are attributed to the relevant authorities or parties until independently established. Election results are described according to their verified status at the time of publication.

breaking.title: Atiku formally launches ADC presidential campaign in Sokoto
breaking.summary: The African Democratic Congress formally flagged off Atiku Abubakar's 2027 presidential campaign in Sokoto on Wednesday, 4 November. Atiku reiterated his commitment to tackling insecurity and presented proposals on economic hardship, petroleum subsidy and border trade. The proposals remain campaign commitments requiring detailed policy explanations.
breaking.imageAlt: Atiku Abubakar at the ADC presidential campaign launch

breaking.title: Police arrest suspect over Peter Obi convoy attack in Calabar
breaking.summary: Cross River State Police confirmed the arrest of a 27-year-old suspect following an attack on Peter Obi's convoy around Watt Market Roundabout in Calabar on 4 November. Police said investigations are continuing to identify other suspected participants and establish the circumstances. The arrested person remains entitled to the presumption of innocence.
breaking.imageAlt: Peter Obi, Nigerian Democratic Congress presidential candidate

breaking.title: Senate scrutinises proposed $7.7 billion external loan
breaking.summary: The Senate has referred President Tinubu's request for approximately $7.7 billion in external borrowing to its Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for examination. The proposed borrowing is intended to help finance the 2026 budget deficit. It has not yet received final legislative approval.
breaking.imageAlt: Nigeria's Senate considers an external borrowing proposal

breaking.title: State police constitutional amendment transmitted to Tinubu
breaking.summary: The National Assembly has transmitted the constitutional amendment seeking to establish state police to President Bola Tinubu for assent after approval by 30 state legislatures. The proposal is not yet operational and requires presidential assent before the constitutional process can be completed.

breaking.title: Democrats take control of both chambers of US Congress
breaking.summary: Democrats secured control of the House of Representatives and Senate in the 3 November midterm elections, according to Reuters. The result creates a major shift in Washington and gives Democrats greater legislative and oversight influence during President Donald Trump's remaining term.

breaking.title: Iran reports fires involving oil tankers and tugboat in Strait of Hormuz
breaking.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reported that two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC gave its account of the vessels' routes and the circumstances. Independent confirmation of the full sequence of events remains necessary.
breaking.imageAlt: Commercial oil tankers navigating the Strait of Hormuz

featured.title: Atiku's Sokoto Campaign: The Rally, the Promises and the Questions Facing Nigeria's 2027 Election
featured.summary: Atiku Abubakar formally launched the ADC presidential campaign in Sokoto on 4 November. The event followed a dispute over campaign facilities and concerns about security. The ADC described the turnout as evidence of public dissatisfaction with the Tinubu administration. Campaign spokesperson Phrank Shaibu also described the scale of the journey and the number of supporters along the route. Such descriptions should be understood as campaign accounts, not independent measurements of national support. Atiku reiterated his commitment to tackling insecurity. His campaign has also discussed restoring petroleum subsidy and reopening land borders for legitimate trade. These proposals require detailed explanations of funding, implementation, economic consequences and safeguards against abuse. The Department of State Services rejected Atiku's allegation that it was recruiting protesters to disrupt the campaign. The agency said its Director-General had ordered an investigation into the allegation. The rally went ahead. The next test for the ADC is to explain how its political promises would translate into measurable public outcomes.
featured.description: A detailed RadiantWaves special report on the ADC campaign launch, Atiku's statements, the security controversy, campaign claims and the policy questions voters should examine.
featured.source: Channels Television; Premium Times; TheCable; Voice of Nigeria

articles.title: Atiku's Sokoto Campaign: What Happened and What Comes Next?
articles.summary: The ADC presidential campaign was formally launched in Sokoto on Wednesday, 4 November. Atiku Abubakar arrived in the state and was received by party leaders and supporters. The rally took place at the ADC state secretariat along Ilorin Road. The campaign described the turnout as a sign of public dissatisfaction with the Tinubu administration. Atiku spoke about insecurity and urged Nigerians to support the ADC. His campaign has also put forward proposals on petroleum subsidy and border trade. These are political commitments that require detailed policy explanations. The event followed a dispute over access to campaign facilities and allegations of political interference. The party's claims about the scale and meaning of the turnout should be understood as campaign statements rather than a nationwide opinion survey.
articles.description: A special report on the campaign launch, the political message, security concerns and policy questions arising from the Sokoto event.
articles.content: The ADC's Sokoto campaign launch marks an important stage in public mobilisation ahead of Nigeria's 2027 general election. Atiku Abubakar said his party would continue its activities despite alleged attempts to frustrate its campaign. The Department of State Services rejected Atiku's allegation that it was recruiting protesters to disrupt the event. The DSS said its operatives had protected ADC governorship candidate Mannir Daniya during an incident on 31 October and that two personnel were injured. It also confirmed that its Director-General had ordered an investigation into Atiku's allegation. The rally proceeded. For voters, the next important issue is the detail behind the promises: security strategy, funding, border management, economic reform and public accountability. The crowd at a political rally can demonstrate enthusiasm among those present, but it cannot by itself establish the level of nationwide electoral support.
articles.source: Channels Television; Premium Times; Voice of Nigeria; TheCable
articles.imageAlt: Atiku Abubakar at the ADC campaign event

articles.title: DSS Rejects Atiku's Allegation and Orders Investigation
articles.summary: The Department of State Services rejected Atiku Abubakar's allegation that it was recruiting protesters to cause unrest in Sokoto. The agency said two of its operatives were injured while protecting ADC governorship candidate Mannir Daniya during an incident on 31 October. The DSS said its Director-General ordered an investigation into Atiku's allegation. The allegation has not been independently established.

articles.title: Peter Obi's Convoy Attacked in Calabar as Police Arrest Suspect
articles.summary: Cross River State Police said suspected hoodlums armed with machetes and sticks attacked Peter Obi's convoy around Watt Market Roundabout in Calabar on 4 November. Police identified an arrested suspect as 27-year-old Victor Edet Yellow Duke. The police said the investigation would continue to identify other participants and establish the circumstances. The arrest is not a determination of guilt, and the suspect remains entitled to the presumption of innocence.

articles.title: Nigeria's State Police Amendment Reaches the Presidency
articles.summary: The National Assembly transmitted the proposed state police constitutional amendment to President Tinubu after 30 state legislatures approved it. The proposal aims to provide a constitutional basis for state police services. Presidential assent is still required, and operational arrangements, funding, recruitment, oversight and safeguards against political interference remain important questions.

articles.title: Tinubu's $7.7 Billion External Borrowing Request Faces Senate Scrutiny
articles.summary: President Bola Tinubu has requested approval for approximately $7.7 billion in external borrowing to part-finance the 2026 budget deficit. The Senate referred the request to its Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for examination. The proposal follows the withdrawal of an earlier, larger external borrowing request. The debate raises questions about debt sustainability, borrowing costs, repayment obligations, transparency and the projects expected to benefit.

articles.title: Democrats Secure Control of Both Chambers of the US Congress
articles.summary: Democrats won control of the House of Representatives and Senate in the 3 November 2026 midterm elections. The result creates a divided-government environment for President Donald Trump during the remaining two years of his term. Reuters reported that voter concerns included the cost of living and the Iran war. The new congressional majority will have greater oversight powers, although the President retains executive authority and veto powers.

articles.title: Iran Reports Fires Involving Two Tankers and a Tugboat in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC said the incidents involved vessels using routes it described as unauthorised and gave an account involving a possible mine strike. These details remain based on the Iranian military's account. Independent confirmation and further information about casualties, vessel identities and the circumstances remain limited.
articles.imageAlt: Oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz

articles.title: Ukraine Reports 40 Deaths After Strike on Aid Distribution Centre
articles.summary: The death toll from a strike on an aid distribution centre and shelter in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, rose to 40 in reports available on 5 November. Ukrainian authorities said people had gathered to receive humanitarian assistance. Russia said it had targeted military units in the area. The competing accounts have not been independently resolved. Rescue and identification operations have continued, while the incident has renewed concern over civilian protection.
articles.imageAlt: Emergency response following a strike in Ukraine

articles.title: France Prepares for Nationwide Demonstrations on 5 November
articles.summary: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez announced that 70,000 police officers and gendarmes would be deployed for Thursday's national day of mobilisation. Authorities expected more than 220 public demonstrations. In Paris, the proposed Bastille-to-Concorde route was rejected and a République-to-Nation route was authorised. Demonstrations are linked to union demands concerning wages and employment. Transport and local conditions may vary by city.

articles.title: Cyberattack Disrupts Refrigeration Controls at French Blood Storage Facilities
articles.summary: France's national blood service said a cyberattack involving a refrigeration equipment provider affected cold-storage facilities at three sites. Temperature and defrosting settings were altered, but monitoring systems detected the anomalies and staff intervened. The blood service said no blood products were lost and no health consequences had been identified. Investigations into the incident are continuing.
articles.imageAlt: Blood storage facilities and medical technology

articles.title: Ethiopia Expels Six Sudanese Diplomatic Staff
articles.summary: Ethiopia ordered six Sudanese diplomatic staff to leave the country, according to a senior Ethiopian official. The move further worsens relations between the neighbours amid allegations that each side is supporting armed groups opposed to the other. Sudan accuses Ethiopia of supporting the Rapid Support Forces, while Ethiopia accuses Sudan of backing rebels in its northern Tigray region. Both sides deny the allegations.

articles.title: British Healthcare Worker with Ebola to Be Evacuated from DR Congo
articles.summary: A British healthcare worker who tested positive for Ebola while supporting the outbreak response in the Democratic Republic of Congo is being evacuated to the United Kingdom for specialist treatment. The patient was reported to be stable. British authorities said the risk to the wider UK public was low. The development highlights the importance of protecting frontline healthcare workers and supporting outbreak response in affected communities.
articles.imageAlt: Ebola response and public health work in the Democratic Republic of Congo

articles.title: South Africa Counts Votes After Municipal Elections
articles.summary: South Africans voted in municipal elections on 4 November, with attention on local service delivery, unemployment, electricity, water and political representation. The Electoral Commission had prepared 23,696 voting stations and reported that polling was scheduled to close at 21:00. Counting and the publication of results are the next stages. Early or partial results should not be presented as final until formally declared by the Electoral Commission.

articles.title: Israel Begins Coalition Consultations After Election Produces No Clear Majority
articles.summary: President Isaac Herzog has accepted the certified results of Israel's parliamentary election and begun consultations with political parties on forming a government. Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot's bloc secured the 61 seats required for a majority in the 120-member Knesset. Coalition negotiations will determine who is best placed to form the next government. A failure to secure a workable majority could lead to another election.
articles.imageAlt: Israeli President Isaac Herzog and parliamentary election developments

articles.title: North Korea Reports New Air Defence Missile Test
articles.summary: North Korea's state media reported that the country tested a newly designed air-defence missile system and conducted a cruise-missile strike drill on Wednesday. The report has been attributed to state media and has not been independently verified. Such tests are likely to draw attention from neighbouring countries and regional security partners.
articles.imageAlt: North Korean missile testing and regional security

articles.title: International Partners Discuss Ukraine's Post-war Reconstruction
articles.summary: European and international representatives met in Brussels to discuss Ukraine's post-war economic development and possible support for reconstruction. The discussions reflect the scale of infrastructure, housing, energy and public-service recovery that would be required after the war. Reconstruction planning does not mean that a peace agreement has been reached.

stories.title: Cybersecurity and France's Blood Storage Infrastructure
stories.summary: A cyberattack involving a refrigeration equipment provider affected temperature-control systems at three French blood-service facilities. Monitoring systems detected the anomalies, staff intervened and the blood service reported that no products were lost. The incident demonstrates how cyber vulnerabilities in third-party suppliers can affect essential public infrastructure.

stories.title: Digital Infrastructure and Public Safety
stories.summary: Healthcare systems, energy networks, transport services and public institutions increasingly depend on connected equipment. Governments and service providers need strong access controls, system monitoring, incident response and contingency arrangements to protect essential services.

thoughtForToday.title: Thought for Today
thoughtForToday.quote: Leadership is not measured by the size of a campaign crowd, but by the quality of decisions, the lives improved and the promises fulfilled.
thoughtForToday.author: RadiantWaves Media Editorial Desk
thoughtForToday.description: A reminder that public leadership should be assessed through measurable results, responsible decisions and accountability.

todaysBigQuestion.title: Today's Big Question
todaysBigQuestion.question: As Nigeria moves towards the 2027 presidential election, what should voters demand from every candidate: a detailed economic plan, a credible security strategy, a record of performance, national unity, or a clear commitment to accountability?
todaysBigQuestion.description: The question applies equally to every political party and every presidential candidate. Citizens should examine policies, records and implementation plans rather than relying only on campaign slogans.

radiantWavesPerspective.title: RadiantWaves Perspective
radiantWavesPerspective.summary: Nigeria's 2027 political contest is entering a more visible campaign phase. Atiku Abubakar's Sokoto rally, Peter Obi's continuing political engagements and the Tinubu administration's policy decisions are all part of a wider national debate. The public deserves clear information about what each political actor proposes and what has actually been delivered. Political competition must remain peaceful, opposition parties must be able to campaign freely, and allegations of intimidation or violence must be investigated impartially. The most important democratic test is whether citizens can make informed choices and hold elected leaders accountable.

sourcePolicy.title: Our Editorial and Verification Policy
sourcePolicy.description: RadiantWaves Media uses attributable reporting from established news organisations, official statements and relevant public institutions. We distinguish verified facts from allegations, campaign claims, forecasts and opinion. Where accounts differ, we identify the parties making the claims and explain what remains unverified. Political promises are reported as promises, not achievements. Developing stories may change as additional information becomes available.
sourcePolicy.verificationNote: This edition reflects reports available during the morning of Thursday, 5 November 2026.
